root_cause.text: The b43legacy RX path uses a firmware-controlled key index without an enforcing bounds check, so an out-of-bounds key index leads to an out-of-bounds read of `dev->key[]` because the existing `B43legacy_WARN_ON` does not prevent execution in production kernels.
root_cause.evidence: The commit description states "the firmware-controlled key index in b43legacy_rx() can exceed dev->max_nr_keys. The existing B43legacy_WARN_ON is non-enforcing in production builds, allowing an out-of-bounds read of dev->key[]. Make the check enforcing by dropping the frame for invalid indices." The patch changes the `B43legacy_WARN_ON(keyidx >= dev->max_nr_keys)` to an `if (B43legacy_WARN_ON(...)) goto drop;`, which drops the frame instead of continuing with an invalid index.
